name: Roach
summary: A worker phenotype emphasizing continuity and bounded recovery.

behavior.target: Resume from durable evidence while preserving the existing owner and budget.
behavior.assay: Compare a source-bound card capsule against matched factual instructions on held-out tasks. Freeze carrier, tools, budget and evaluator; record constraint violations, useful outcomes and operator corrections. See /cards/behavior-assay.json.

runtime.note: Source engineering maturity is a historical author assertion, not fresh runtime evidence.

art.prompt: Original HFO editorial science-fantasy. Obsidian, restrained crimson light, ivory highlights, etched technical geometry, tactile mineral and archival-paper textures. Vertical 4:5, one clear central silhouette, quiet crop margins. No text, numerals, logos, badges, evidence stamps, franchise characters or recognizable franchise art. Conceptual illustration only. Subject: Roach. Show a compact modular seed-engine with visible attachment points. Express the intended role without depicting deployment, victory or authority.
art.alt: Planned conceptual illustration for Roach; no artwork generated.

behavior_contract.intent: Candidate behavior: carry unfinished work through interruption without losing identity or repeating uncertain effects.
behavior_contract.when_to_use: When resuming a bounded task from durable evidence after an attempt ends.
inputs: Original WorkItem, ownership/lease evidence and remaining budget
Last durable checkpoint, candidate artifacts and effect observations
procedure: Reconstruct completed, pending and uncertain steps from the checkpoint and artifacts.
Reconcile ownership and uncertain effects through permitted evidence before retrying.
Choose one continuation step within the original ceiling and remaining budget.
Return a new checkpoint, exact output references and a bounded next-action handoff.
outputs: Recovery plan tied to the original work identity
Updated checkpoint candidate and unresolved-effect list

example.situation: An extraction attempt ends after saving part of its output.
example.action: Compare the saved artifact with required fields and continue only the missing portion under valid ownership.
example.evidence: Expected: original identity, prior checkpoint, preserved completed output and independently checked continuation.

neurosymbolic.neural: Diagnose the interruption and select a useful recovery step.
neurosymbolic.symbolic: Preserve ownership, checkpoints, effect history and budget accounting.

mutable: Checkpoint clarity and bounded recovery heuristics
frozen: Work identity, ownership rules and effect ceiling
evolution.fitness: Evaluate recovered useful output, duplicate effects and operator intervention under fixed interruption cases.
